newsitem.title: USA: Cancer genome Web site to aid research.
newsitem.headline: Cancer genome Web site to aid research.

text.p: A new Internet site aimed at helping researchers learn more about genetic links to cancer was unveiled on Friday by Vice President Al Gore and others.
The site, developed by the National Cancer Institute and the National Library of Medicine, will allow researchers to ask specific questions about genes involved in the development of cancer.

Gore, at a ceremony in the Old Executive Office Building, across from the White House, likened various forms of cancer listed at the site -- ranging from lymph, lung and breast to ovarian and bone marrow -- to a "most wanted" poster and said the new site would help scientists learn more about genetic aspects of these diseases.
The Web site can be accessed at www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/ncicgap.
